\section[(with a clock)]{The same writing, with a clock}

\label{lesson:PT-W257-with-a-clock}



\begin{quote}
You wrote your own line with as long as you liked.

A task you can only do untimed is not yet a task you can do.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Writing — timed production}
\textbf{What CAPLE publishes.} This track's A1 target is \textbf{ACESSO}, from CAPLE at the University of Lisbon. It certifies \textbf{A1} in \textbf{four components}, over about \textbf{one hour and thirty-five minutes}, and a pass is any overall result from \textbf{55\% to 100\%}.

\textbf{What this page does not quote.} This book has not checked how many minutes ACESSO gives its writing component, or how many words it asks for, so it gives you no such number.

\textbf{What this book's own A1 paper sets.} Twenty minutes, in two parts: a practical form, then a 30–40 word message to a named reader. That shape is the project's own, read out of \texttt{task-shapes/a1.json}. It is not CAPLE's.

Today, the first part only, against a short clock. Set a three-minute timer, then fill six fields, in Portuguese:

\begin{enumerate}
\raggedright
  \item your name;
  \item the city where you live;
  \item one language you speak;
  \item the city where you work;
  \item one day of the week you work;
  \item a number from one to ten, as a word.
\end{enumerate}

When the three-minute timer rings, \textbf{stop}, even mid-word.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Spend at most one minute checking. The marks come first: the accent on a day or a number, and the hyphen before \textbf{feira}.

Now the rule worth carrying out of this lesson, because it changes how you study rather than how you write today.

CAPLE passes ACESSO on \textbf{one overall figure, 55\%}, across the four components. A strong reader can carry a weak writer.

This book's contract is stricter: \textbf{60\% on every paper, each on its own}, and no total makes up for a paper that falls short. Study for the stricter rule. If writing is your weak paper, reading practice does not repair it.
\end{tcolorbox}
